chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to write to his officials: 'Do not conscript the Muslims [for forced labor]; and whoever asks you for something other than the obligatory tax, he has exceeded [his right], so do not give it to him.' And he used to write advising kindness to the peasants, and they are the hired laborers.
ai.seo_question: What were Imam Ali's instructions to his governors regarding forced labor and extra taxes?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) fiscal justice by prohibiting the imposition of forced labor (*khuraj*) on Muslims and defining any demand beyond the fixed obligatory dues (*fard*) as an administrative overreach (*i'tada*). It further underscores the ethical governance of agricultural workers (*akkaron*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on equitable economic administration and the protection of the common populace from arbitrary exactions.
